slides.title: Cold showers won't "reset" your p*rn brain. [[Here's what actually helps.]]
The [[hype]]
slides.body: "Cold showers boost dopamine 250%." "7-day dopamine detox." Many viral p*rn-quitting claims aren't backed by solid research.

slides.title: Hacks aren't a [[plan]]
slides.body: A cold shower can help you ride out one p*rn urge. Great. But no single trick fixes p*rn addiction on its own.

slides.title: What [[does]] help
slides.body: Removing easy access to p*rn, knowing your triggers, support from other people and time. Boring? Yes. Effective? Also yes.

slides.title: P*rn is filling [[one of these 4 needs.]]
slides.sub: Fix the need, and the p*rn urge gets quieter.

slides.title: [[Rest]]
slides.body: Exhausted and drained, p*rn feels like switching off. What you actually need: sleep, a real break, doing nothing for a while.

slides.title: [[Connection]]
slides.body: Lonely or disconnected, p*rn offers fake closeness. What you actually need: a call, a friend, people who know you.

slides.title: [[Relief]]
slides.body: Stressed or anxious, p*rn is a quick escape. What you actually need: movement, breathing, talking it out.

slides.title: [[Excitement]]
slides.body: Bored with life, p*rn gives instant novelty. What you actually need: a challenge, a goal, something to build.

slides.title: Quitting p*rn — but your group chat [[keeps sending it.]]
slides.sub: How to handle friends without losing them.

slides.title: It's a real [[trigger]]
slides.body: Memes, clips, "look at this" links. One tap and you're back on p*rn. It counts as a trigger, even when it's "just a joke."

slides.title: Mute, don't [[leave]]
slides.body: You don't need to quit your friends to quit p*rn. Mute the chat, turn off media auto-download and check it on your terms.

slides.title: Say [[something]]
slides.body: "I'm off p*rn for a while — keep that stuff out of here for me?" Good friends will respect it. Some might even join you.

slides.title: Your p*rn blocker has [[holes in it.]]
slides.sub: 4 loopholes your brain will find at 1 AM.

slides.title: [[Mobile data]]
slides.body: Some network-level p*rn filters only work on Wi-Fi. Switch to mobile data and the block is gone.

slides.title: "Restricted" [[isn't blocked]]
slides.body: Restricted modes on video apps filter some content — they're not a full p*rn blocker. Don't rely on them alone.

slides.title: Other [[browsers]] & apps
slides.body: A second browser, a private window, an app you forgot about. If your p*rn blocker only covers one, you'll find the other.

slides.title: You know the [[password]]
slides.body: If you can switch off your own p*rn blocker in 10 seconds, so can your 1 AM self. Let someone else hold the passcode.

Late night? After work? Sunday evening?

slides.title: [[Places]]
slides.body: Bed? Bathroom? Desk with the door closed? The places where you usually watch p*rn become triggers on their own.

slides.title: [[Feelings]]
slides.body: Bored, stressed, lonely, rejected, celebrating. Most p*rn urges are a feeling looking for an exit.

slides.body:
